segments.text: What if you lived on a world spinning so fast it stretched into an egg?
Far beyond Neptune, there's a dwarf planet that spins like crazy. Its name is Haumea.
segments.headline: A spinning world

segments.text: One day on Haumea lasts about three point nine hours. One of the fastest spins of any big object in the solar system.
All that spinning stretched it into an egg. About two thousand three hundred kilometers long, but only about one thousand kilometers thick.
Scientists think a giant collision long ago set it spinning, and threw off pieces that still follow it today.
segments.headline: A giant crash

segments.text: In twenty seventeen, Haumea passed in front of a star. The star blinked out before and after the planet. Haumea has a ring!
segments.headline: Surprise: a ring

segments.text: It was the first ring ever found around a dwarf planet.

visual.label: ring discovered
visual.sub: a first for a dwarf planet

segments.text: Haumea also has two moons, named Hi'iaka and Namaka, after daughters of the Hawaiian goddess Haumea.
segments.headline: Two moons

segments.text: Its surface shines with fresh crystal water ice.
segments.headline: Covered in ice
